messages:
alex: quick heads-up — I hit a big perf cliff when host->GPU transfers start interleaving with eviction. tail latency spikes and token throughput halves :grimacing:

alex: repro: feed a steady stream of 8k sequences with small batch sizes, then hammer the memory budget to force eviction. attaching a few logs below.

alex: `EVICT start (alloc=1.9G) -> stall 45ms -> GPU memcpy queued -> eviction done -> memcpy resumes`

maria: can you paste the pmap/nvidia-smi snapshot? also which allocator path (slab/segmented)?

alex: nvidia-smi shows 12GB used, host staging increases ~700MB during eviction window. allocator=segmented, host-staging pool enabled.

ryan: sounds like backpressure at DMA queueing — eviction blocks the transfer thread. two quick models: 1) block incoming requests until eviction completes (simpler, higher p99), 2) allow transfer but use syncpoints/credits to limit concurrent DMA and let evict run async.

sarah: option 2 is nicer for latency but is hairy: fragmentation risk if we keep admitting new allocations while evicting. we'd need a compact-defrag or aggressive coalesce on the allocator.

devon: what about a credit-based gate at the allocator boundary? allocator hands out a "DMA token" per allocation. when free tokens are 0, callers either queue or go to host-staging. evict reclaims tokens when pages freed. minimal invasive change.

maria: +1 on token idea. but need clear ownership: is token logic in the allocator or eviction manager? keep allocator pure for alloc/free, put gating in eviction manager with callbacks?

ryan: interface boundary: allocator exposes `try_reserve(size) -> handle|ENOSPC`, and can call `register_eviction_candidate(handle)`. eviction manager owns eviction policy & backpressure. allocator should remain ignorant of higher-level request flow.

alex: that design keeps invariants separated. downside: more cross-component callbacks and harder to reason about corner cases during crash/restart. also need metrics: outstanding_tokens, avg_wait_ms, evict_latency.

sarah: fragmentation concern again — even with tokens, long-running allocations can leave many small holes. propose an async background compaction thread that operates only on cold regions and exposes `compact_hint(range)`. we can mark hot allocations pinned so compaction skips them.

devon: compaction + credit gating + eviction worker seems like the trifecta. Implementation plan: Phase 1: credit gate + simple eviction worker (LIFO), Phase 2: background compactor + pinned hot list, Phase 3: refine eviction policy with workload signals (seq_len distribution).

ryan: also consider graceful fallback: if eviction + compaction can't keep up, route requests to cheaper quantized model or spill to dedicated host-pool. keep SLOs via routing layer.

alex: agreed. owners? I can draft an RFC that describes token API, eviction manager callbacks, and metrics. devon can prototype the token gate. sarah can sketch compactor constraints.

maria: please include microbenchmarks — small batch vs large batch, short vs long sequences. we should measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec with and without gate.

deploybot: canary: evict-token-gate v1 rolled to infra-test cluster (shard-3) at 1905012375 :rocket:

alex: sweet — i'll watch the logs and post a follow-up. next: RFC in #eng-runtime by EOD Tue. :thumbsup:

maria: :thinking: one more item — ensure KMS/HSM pinned pages aren't accidentally evictable. add policy flag `non_evictable` on handles.

devon: noted, add to RFC.

alex: thanks all, closing thread once RFC is up.
